full_judgment: 5. The trial Court decreed the suit on the finding that the plaintiffs are entitled to benevolent fund and group insurance as per provision of section 23(c) of Ordinance No. XXXIX of 1982, hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance of 1982, and that acceptance of the benefit by the plaintiffs already paid to them would not dis-entitle them to get the benefit of benevolent fund and group insurance under the Ordinance of 1982, that the plaintiffs' suit is maintainable and not barred by limitation, that the defendants would make payment to the plaintiffs under the existing law upon adjustment of the benefit already paid to plaintiffs and received by them. The defendants went on appeal. The appellate Court allowed the appeal upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the findings that the plaintiffs will not get the benefit of group insurance and benevolent fund as per provision of section 23(c) and (d) of the Ordinance of 1982 and that claim of benefit by the plaintiffs upon placing reliance on the aforesaid provisions of law is misconceived, that plaintiffs upon receiving the benefit under the old law waived their right to have their benefits under the new law and, as such, their claims made in the suit were not entertainable in law, that plaintiffs predecessor having had died in 1969 the plaintiffs were entitled to the benefit as per the law or laws as was or were in force at that time that the declaratory relief sought by the plaintiffs is not sustainable in law that the plaintiffs' suit was barred under sections 11 and 12 of EP Ordinance No. III of 1968 and section 13 of EP Ordinance No. XI of 1969.
